title: POC weekly sync - reliability incident followup
summary: Weekly POC sync to review the reliability incident from earlier in the week (intermittent 5xx/timeouts under burst load). Went over initial post-incident traces, rate limiting behavior, retry/backoff tuning, and next steps for targeted load tests and logs sharing.
next_steps: Redwood to share filtered traces and Grafana dashboard link (logs.redwood/bluewave-poc)
Customer to run targeted burst load test and share results by 2026-03-16
Carlos (SE) to propose retry/backoff config and autoscale tweak by 2026-03-15
action_items: Carlos Ruiz (SE): collect and share request/response traces, KV cache hit rates, and GPU utilization from incident window (due: 2026-03-15)
Jenna Lee (ML Eng): run the provided burst test script against staging and upload results to shared spreadsheet (due: 2026-03-16)
Maya Patel (AE): share pricing note for temporary increased burst capacity and Dedicated slot options (due: 2026-03-14)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-12 10:00am PT — Duration: ~40 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Jenna Lee (BlueWave ML), Marcus Cho (BlueWave Platform), Priya Nair (BlueWave Product)

00:00 Maya: okay hi everyone thanks for joining today's POC weekly, we'll focus on the reliability incident from tuesday and make sure we have concrete next steps. carlos and i will run through what we saw.
00:14 Carlos: yeah hi, quick recap — we saw a burst around 13:12 UTC on tuesday, roughly a 7 minute window where we saw increased latency and a spike of 5xxs, mostly 503/504s. manifests as client timeouts and some requests being rate limited. some notes — i pulled the shard logs and there were a couple of retry storms.
00:37 Jenna: yep that matches our observability, we saw production spikes in our async job processing and noticed a lot of queued requests hitting the inference endpoint which then returned 504 after 30s.
00:51 Marcus: just to add, our autoscaler didn't kick as expected, looks like the Dedicated pool hit a soft cap then the fallback routing sent traffic to hosted variant and that caused a SLO gap.
01:06 Carlos: correct — root cause seems multi-factor: burst traffic pattern from customer side + conservative autoscale threshold + default rate-limiter on hosted side. also KV cache warming was low so per-request compute cost rose.
01:22 Maya: okay, can you show the traces quickly?
01:25 Carlos: sure — i shared a link in the chat to the filtered traces and the grafana dash (logs.redwood/bluewave-poc). see this trace here, you can see the first attempt failed with 503, client retried immediately and we observed 10x amplification on the same key space. the K-V cache reads were low, we mis-identified some prefix caching due to session mismatch — the transcription in some of the auto text says "K-V cash" but it's KV cache.
01:55 Jenna: small note — our client SDK does retries on 5xx with linear backoff, default 0.5s then 1s then 1s, maybe that made it worse?
02:09 Carlos: yeah precisely. immediate retries without exponential backoff turned a recoverable error into a retry storm. recommended change is exponential backoff with jitter and an upper cap.
02:22 Priya: is there anything from Redwood side we should tweak? like rate limit increases or queue sizing?
02:27 Maya: two levers — temporary higher burst capacity on Dedicated (we can enable for short windows), and tuning the hosted rate-limiter thresholds. tradeoff is cost vs risk — increasing burst limits will raise spend but reduces 5xx risk.
02:44 Marcus: for POC we can accept a brief cost bump if it stabilizes the service for demo traffic. what's the effort to enable temporary burst capacity?
02:52 Maya: i can enable a short burst within a day, but i'll need sign-off and we'll show cost estimate. i'll share a small pricing note after this call.
03:03 Carlos: on the infra side, we recommend these actions now: 1) client-side: exponential backoff + jitter; 2) server-side: adjust rate-limiter to prefer 429 over immediate 503 when overloaded; 3) short-term: enable a higher Dedicated burst pool; 4) medium-term: add circuit breaker on client to stop aggressive retries and queue requests with backpressure.
03:29 Jenna: for the client change, how are you recommending we set the values?
03:33 Carlos: start with base 200ms, multiply by 2, cap at 4s, add full jitter. limit retries to 3. that avoids tight retry loops. we'll provide a reference config.
03:47 Priya: do we need to change model variant or quantization profile?
03:51 Carlos: not necessary for this incident; most of the increased latency was due to cache misses and concurrency surge. changing model quantization won't fix the retry storm. however, we will also look at batching and continuous batching knobs in Redwood Optimize recommendations to improve token throughput.
04:10 Maya: any security/compliance asks tied to the logs we shared? bluewave — we redacted PII but can do more if needed.
04:18 Marcus: logs look fine, we just need shortened retention for dev traces. also please confirm KMS and encryption at rest for the private pilot.
04:27 Maya: yes KMS and encryption are on for your Private deployment; i'll attach the security doc in the CRM.
04:33 Carlos: quick question — during the incident we saw fallback routing to hosted which had a slightly different model version. could that cause inference errors?
04:41 Jenna: we saw some small differences in tokenization and a few hallucinations but the biggest user-visible was latency/timeouts.
04:50 Carlos: okay so actionables — i'll collect more detailed traces including request timestamps, cache hits, and GPU utilization; maya will share burst pricing; jenn a will run the burst test script we provided and upload results.
05:05 Priya: what's the follow up cadence?
05:08 Maya: we'll reconvene next wednesday but i propose an incident review meeting on 2026-03-18 to go over the updated traces and postmortem.
05:16 Jenna: fine. one more thing — can you share the benchmark spreadsheet and the load test script?
05:21 Maya: yes shared: https://redwood.app/bluewave/poc-bench and the script in the chat.
05:28 Marcus: last question — if we need longer term stability, is Dedicated the recommended path?
05:33 Carlos: for predictable latency and controlled isolation, yes Dedicated with pinned model versions and configured autoscale policies is the right long-term solution. hosted works for burstable, but platform teams may prefer Dedicated for SLAs.
05:45 Maya: ok to recap next steps: carlos to send traces and config suggestions, jenn to run burst tests, maya to send pricing and security link, schedule incident review 2026-03-18. any objections?
05:58 Jenna: none. thanks all.
06:01 Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links and action items. bye.
file_notes: Reference links and artifacts mentioned in transcript: grafana/gc traces and 'poc-bench' spreadsheet. transcript contains some auto-transcription errors especially around acronyms (KV cache written as K-V cash) which are typical of Fireflies exports.
